genevn-g.name: Motorola G Stylus 5G 2023
genevn-g.android_version_note: android14 = the ROM this unit runs now, not its KMI and not the release it launched on. This device launched on Android 12; docs claiming Android 13 are wrong. SM6450 on a 5.10 vendor tree is GKI 1.0: its KMI list is android/abi_gki_aarch64_moto, which ships in android12-5.10 and not android13-5.10. This build clones kernel_source and never derives VERSION_DIR, so patch-directory resolution does not affect it.
genevn-g.kernel_tree_note: AR-NUKI-genevn is the real genevn kernel tree (5.10.240, arch/arm64 + drivers present, fs/susfs.c and fs/zeromount.c already in-tree). The previous value kernel-msm-1 was wrong: that repo carries only README.md, CROSS_REFERENCES.md and fs/koto/ -- it is the source repo in the Colonel chain, not buildable. kernel-zenith is the separate x86_64 tree for the DarkMatter ISO and must not be used for this device.
genevn-g.build_target_note: NUKI = Native Unified Kernel Image, NURFS = Native Unified Root File System. One kernel image built whole from AR-NUKI-genevn with the user space integrated natively -- no chroot, proot, container or libc translator. This is NOT a GKI build: there is no KMI to match and no separately-built vendor module set. The android_version field records lineage (what the tree derives from), not a Google branch being built.
genevn-g.edition_note: The mobile edition of AnyRealm: the same NUKI/NURFS architecture on arm64, packaged as a flashable kernel instead of an ISO.

board._note: Read from BoardConfigCommon.mk of android_device_motorola_sm6450-common@lineage-23.0, not guessed.

trees._note: Every piece forked for this device, verified with git ls-remote on 2026-11-17. `parent` is where the fork came from, recorded so a future rebase has a target.

parents.android_device_motorola_genevn: Satan19/android_device_motorola_yume (deleted from GitHub; fork is the only copy)

declared_but_missing._note: The common device tree's lineage.dependencies names these four, and none exists upstream at any of the three plausible owners (015stray91, moto-common, LineageOS). This is the concrete reason AR-NUKI-genevn is self-sufficient: the tree it would have fetched does not exist.
declared_but_missing.consequence: TARGET_KERNEL_SOURCE in BoardConfig points at kernel/motorola/sm7435 and the dependency list asks for sm6450; neither kernel repo exists, so the vendor tree alone cannot produce a kernel. AR-NUKI-genevn supplies that half.

ar_nuki_build_config._note: AR-NUKI-genevn still contains build.config.* files, including build.config.anyrealm.kernel. They are inert: the tree does not invoke them and nothing outside it overrides the build. The claim of severance is about behaviour, not about the absence of filenames.

identity._note: Reconciled 2026-11-17 by reading the trees, not by guessing. Three names refer to the one phone, and they are not synonyms: each is a different layer.
identity.consequence: AnyKernel device check must accept all four aliases, because the recovery tree accepts all four. A kernel that flashes only on 'genevn' would refuse a package built for a unit that reports 'yume'.

darkmatter-vivobook.name: ASUS Vivobook Go 14/15 (DarkMatter + NetHunter Pro)
darkmatter-vivobook.base_os_note: android_version records where the KERNEL TREE came from (kernel-zenith is based on Google android16-6.12), NOT the OS in the ISO. The ISO runs DarkMatter Exo 4.7, which is Android-x86 7.1.1. The kernel is built monolithic x86_64 with KMI_GENERATION=0 and no GKI module split, so the android<NN>-<KMI> release-string suffix that arm64 GKI kernels get does not apply here.
darkmatter-vivobook.build_target_note: NUKI/NURFS on x86_64: kernel-zenith 6.12 built whole, DarkMatter rootfs with the Kali user space merged into it at build time, one kernel and one user space. Not a GKI build and not Android-x86 stock -- the ISO base is DarkMatter Exo 4.7 (Android-x86 7.1.1) but the result is a native unified image.
darkmatter-vivobook.edition_note: The desktop edition of AnyRealm. The deliverable is a bootable x86_64 install ISO: kernel-zenith 6.12 built whole as NUKI, DarkMatter Exo 4.7 rootfs with the Kali NetHunter Pro user space merged in as NURFS. Boots from USB on the Vivobook Go 14/15, which is UEFI-only.

_project.name: AnyRealm
_project.about: AnyRealm is the project identity. NUKI (Native Unified Kernel Image) and NURFS (Native Unified Root File System) are how it is built: one kernel compiled whole from one tree, one user space integrated natively, no chroot/proot/container/translator, no KMI to match at boot.
